permissionModes.ask: session rules: reads allow; shell, edits, web and external paths ask; configured denies stay
permissionModes.full: session rules: allow all except configured denies; stray requests allow once

permissions.networkControl: OpenCode session permission rules (web fetch and search ask in Ask), read back before each run
knownLimitations: OpenCode has no automatic reviewer, so Approve for me is unavailable.
OpenCode has no OS sandbox: Ask confines tools with OpenCode's own permission rules, and an approved shell command runs unconfined.

Allow for session is a LUNA-owned rule on the chat's OpenCode session, never an OpenCode saved rule: it lasts until LUNA restarts or the chat's permission mode changes, and covers the session that asked (a sub-agent's grant stays with that sub-agent).
Native sub-agents are capped at the chat's mode when OpenCode creates them; their own agent restrictions and your configured OpenCode denies stay in force.

unsupported.reason: OpenCode has no automatic reviewer, so Approve for me is unavailable.
OpenCode keeps no file checkpoints LUNA can restore; a rewind keeps the files.
A model or effort change applies to the chat's next turn.

limitations: The worker hosts LUNA's own OpenCode 2 adapter (HTTP and SSE to `opencode serve --stdio`). OpenCode 1.x and ACP are not supported.

Each turn runs in its own worker with its own `opencode serve` process and port; Stop, a crash or a resource limit ends only that turn. Model discovery, titles, commands, history, fork, rewind and the compaction of an idle chat share one worker.

The worker inherits LUNA's environment like the built-in adapter it replaces, so OpenCode sees the same provider keys, configuration and data directories, and signs in with its own accounts (`opencode auth login`).
A turn's worker group may use at most 4 GiB of memory and 64 processes; past that LUNA ends that turn.
